title: year
summary: Extract calendar year components from datetime values with MATLAB-compatible output shaping.

gpu_support.notes: datetime values are host-side objects; `year` reads the stored serial-date data on the CPU.

description: `year(t)` extracts year numbers from datetime values and retained legacy date inputs, returning double values with the input shape.
behaviors: `year(t)` accepts datetime scalars and arrays. The optional year type is `'iso'` or `'gregorian'`.
For compatibility with existing code, serial date numbers and text dates are also accepted; an optional date format can be supplied for legacy input.
The output shape matches the input shape.
The returned values are numeric doubles, even when the years are mathematically integers.
RunMat mode additionally accepts single-precision and native integer legacy serial-date storage.

examples.description: Extract the year from a scalar datetime
Extract years from a datetime array

faqs.question: Does `year` preserve the input shape?
faqs.answer: Yes. A scalar datetime returns a scalar double, and datetime arrays return numeric arrays of the same size.

faqs.question: Does `year` return integers?
faqs.answer: It returns MATLAB-style doubles whose values are whole-number years.

faqs.question: Does `year` run on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. datetime values are host-side objects, so `year` executes on the CPU.

gpu_residency: No. `year` reads datetime objects on the CPU and returns ordinary host-side numeric arrays.
gpu_behavior: `year` does not dispatch GPU kernels. If the datetime was produced from gathered numeric data, the result still remains a CPU numeric array.
